novelty_basis: Searches (2026-10-18) for the Zeckendorf game together with lazy representations / chip-firing found no such statement; the papers on the game (Baird-Smith et al. arXiv:1809.04881; Li et al. arXiv:2006.16457; Cusenza et al. arXiv:2009.09510; Cheigh et al. 2025; Black Hole Zeckendorf games arXiv:2409.10981) do not mention lazy representations. Small; uses the classical uniqueness of lazy representations (J. L. Brown, 1965).
proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C19.md Theorem 2 - abelian property, an explicit carry lemma by induction, increment of the lazy representation); verified for every n < 5000 and for 300 random firing orders (EXP-C19-02); skeptic-reviewed 2026-10-18 (reviews/skeptic_C13_C19.md) - from every position of value <= 200 all maximal split sequences have one end point and one length
statement:
From n copies of F_1, every maximal sequence of split moves (F_1 + F_1 -> F_2, F_2 + F_2 -> F_1 + F_3,
F_i + F_i -> F_{i-2} + F_{i+1}) has the same length and ends at the lazy representation of n - the unique
representation as a sum of distinct F_i (F_1 = 1, F_2 = 2, ...) without two consecutive missing indices below
the largest one.
title: The split phase of the longest game ends at the lazy Fibonacci representation
